utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Could it be Trivic? T-R-I --

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Something like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: What happened after you received these assignments?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC
utterances.text: The 10th, the 10th in the evening.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I'm referring to the 11th.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC
utterances.text: The 11th, that was already in the afternoon. From their initial positions, units of the tactical group started moving towards Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And did you arrive in Srebrenica with your unit?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Why not?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC
utterances.text: Just before the attack, or, rather, just before the units of the tactical group of the Zvornik Brigade started to move, there was an air strike against our units and our positions. It was a NATO air strike in several waves and in one such attack, a vehicle of the medical corps was damaged as well as the vehicle of the commander of the Podrinje Detachment. I was in the vicinity and I suffered some shell shock, so I was sent to the medical unit in Zeleni Jadar.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. And did you remain there?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC
utterances.text: I have to say before I was sent for treatment, I had spent quite a lot of time with the commander and unit commanders, and it was only when I started feeling the consequences of that explosion, perhaps an hour or two later, that I was sent to the medical unit, and I stayed in Zeleni Jadar until the next morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. The next morning, can you tell us what happened? This is the morning of the 12th.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC
utterances.text: On the morning of the 12th, I already knew that our units had entered Srebrenica because the commander arrived in Zeleni Jadar where the logistics of our unit was positioned. He was on some assignment and he also went to see me, so when he finished his business, I returned together with the commander to Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. And where in Srebrenica did you go with the commander?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC
utterances.text: On the Zeleni Jadar-Rajna village-Bojna village-Srebrenica road.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Now, when you say commander, are you referring to Commander Pandurevic?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Commander Pandurevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And did you discuss anything with Commander Pandurevic during the trip to Srebrenica from Zeleni Jadar?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. We talked. We talked about the things that happened after I was sent to Zeleni Jadar, how the units entered Srebrenica, and all the things that transpired until we met up again.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And can you recall specifically what the commander told you?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC
utterances.text: Well, he was saying that at the outset there was some resistance from the 28th Division, but it was practically non-existent towards the end so that our units entered Srebrenica without encountering any resistance, that the tactical group entered the town, the units were stationed in surrounding buildings to secure the units that were in Srebrenica. And after that, he had gone to Bratunac on the Srebrenica-Potocari-Bratunac road.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Did he mention to you why he went to Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC
utterances.text: He went to a meeting that was convened by General Mladic and General Krstic.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And did he mention to you what was discussed at that meeting?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC
utterances.text: To submit reports on missions accomplished and the missions that might follow after the taking of Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. Did he mention to you what missions might follow after the taking of Srebrenica at that time?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC
utterances.text: Well, from what I understood, it was evident that the units of the 28th Division had retreated from Srebrenica but they only pulled out of the town. So there was combat in prospect to the west of town because the units of the 28th Division were still there. They had not been crushed. And that was probably going to determine our next assignments.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And did he mention what time this meeting was?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC
utterances.text: I'm not sure. It was some time in the evening. Or at night.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And other than commanders General Mladic, General Krstic, Commander Pandurevic, did he mention who else was at this meeting?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC
utterances.text: I don't remember. I suppose there were other unit commanders, commanders of units of tactical group strength or brigade strength. I can only suppose but I really don't remember the names.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Following your arrival in Srebrenica, what happened?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC
utterances.text: The commander brought me to a suburb called Gostilj, where after moving from the police station, a new base was set up for the tactical group.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. And what happened while you were in Gostilj?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC
utterances.text: Gostilj. We were awaiting assignments. We were awaiting a specific assignment for Tactical Group 1. We were resting, talking, waiting for new orders.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And did those new orders come at some point?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. They did. Tactical Group 1 was ordered to be prepared as backup for Tactical Group 2, which was going to search the terrain, as the terminology went, on the axis Srebrenica-Viogor village-Suceska village.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Did you receive these orders at a meeting or some other way?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC
utterances.text: The orders were handed down. When the commander gathered all the company commanders and that one platoon commander, he told them that they should gather their troops, prepare a column for march, and start moving towards Suceska. I don't remember any messengers coming.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And do you remember who was there?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC
utterances.text: All the commanders of companies and the commander of the Podrinje Detachment.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Did you receive any specific orders from your commander following this gathering or meeting?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC
utterances.text: My orders were to prepare my unit for march.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: What happened after that?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC
utterances.text: When we had formed a marching column, we started moving with the commander in his vehicle, in the direction of Srebrenica, Viogor, Suceska, and when we started it was around 1200 hours, and we reached our destination at around 1400 hours, maybe 1500 hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And did you participate in any combat operations while on this march?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC
utterances.text: Not during the march. There was no fighting.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: What happened after you arrived at your destination in Suceska?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC
utterances.text: We didn't go to Suceska. We stopped at the Viogor pass where upon the orders of General Krstic we stayed, awaiting new assignments.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And from the time that you left Srebrenica to the time that you arrived in Viogor, were you with your commander?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, with the commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And were you in contact with the corps command during that period of time?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC
utterances.text: I was not. My position did not enable me to communicate with the corps command unless the commander decides otherwise.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. And what about your commander? Was he in contact with the corps command?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC
utterances.text: When we arrived in the Viogor sector, we received an order to stay there, which means that in one way or another the commander had received an order for us not to proceed towards Suceska village but to keep the unit in the general sector of that Viogor pass, Siljato Hill and Jahorina. This is the general area that I'm talking about.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. Is that what happened? Did you stay in that area?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. That's where we stayed. We did not proceed any further.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And what happened after you were -- you received the order to stay?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC
utterances.text: We started arranging our ranks, replenishing the unit because an order could have been received any moment for us to proceed with the combat activities. We talked to the commanders and we did the usual things that a commander would normally do whenever a unit stopped for a rest and when it wasn't engaged in combat activities.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. And what happened after that, later in the day?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC
utterances.text: Sometime in the afternoon, around 1700 hours or maybe 1800 hours, the Chief of Staff arrived in the Viogor sector. This was the chief of the staff of the corps, General Krstic.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And what happened after General Krstic arrived in Viogor?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC
utterances.text: General Krstic had a conversation with the commander and during that conversation he made us understand that in the Suceska sector there were no units of the 28th Division, that this division had moved northward in the direction of Jaglici village and that we should keep our unit in the Viogor sector and that we should prepare our unit to spend the night there.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] And was there any indication as to what would be the anticipated next course of action for your unit?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC
utterances.text: As regards the 28th Division? Or the following day? What did you have in mind.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Let me rephrase the question because I see also the transcript says that my mike isn't on. Did you -- did you have any indication as to what your unit was supposed to do next or could expect to do next following General Krstic's visit?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC
utterances.text: There were indications that we would prepare our unit to proceed with combat activities in the Zepa sector.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC
utterances.text: However, we did not receive any concrete orders or tasks with regard Zepa, no concrete tasks were given to us by General Krstic.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. This was on the 12th, the evening or afternoon of the 12th; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC
utterances.text: On the 12th, in the evening of that day, yes. Or late in the afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And around what time did General Krstic leave?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC
utterances.text: It may have been around 1700 or 1800 hours. He spent some time with us because we had gathered the command of our unit and the Chief of Staff attended our meeting in order to listen to some of our problems that we were supposed to deal with in order to prepare our unit for anything that might have followed, any combat activities in the future. He may have stayed for about half an hour or so.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Was there any member of the command of the second tactical group present at that meeting?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC
utterances.text: There were some troops of the Tactical Group 2 from the Bircani Brigade but I don't remember that our meeting was attended by the commander of the 2nd Romanija -- i.e. the commander of that tactical group, group 2. I -- somehow my memory fails me on that. I can't remember him being there.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. Following that meeting, were there any other meetings held on the 12th of July?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC
utterances.text: Only in our unit? I don't know about any other units, only in our unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. Involving your unit. Was there any other meeting following this one that was attended by General Krstic?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC
utterances.text: Only our command and commanders of the subordinate units.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. And where was that meeting?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC
utterances.text: In the Viogor pass, Siljato Brdo, Jahorina sector where our troops were deployed at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. And around what time was that meeting?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC
utterances.text: Once the Chief of Staff, Krstic, left, once the meeting that gathered all the commanders ended and General Krstic left, maybe an hour after that.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And do you recall what was discussed at that meeting?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC
utterances.text: Tactical Group 2, which was a temporary unit and not very used to continuous combat activities and had suffered certain losses, required some more work in order to be able to prepare for the ensuing combat activities. The commander always had ways and means how to prepare any unit to continue its engagements, the engagements that lie ahead. And that's exactly what we did on that occasion.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. And so for both of these meetings, was your commander present?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, he was.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And do you know of any other meeting that occurred that evening or that night involving your commander or the command of your unit?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC
utterances.text: No, not now, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And that night, did you remain in Viogor? That is, the unit.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC
utterances.text: We deployed our units and we set up a camp for the command and the commanders and all the units that were on the strength of our tactical group. It was a rather tall order to set up a camp for 400 men.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Where was the camp set up, in Viogor?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC
utterances.text: On the Viogor pass exactly, left to the Srebrenica-Viogor-Milici road.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I'd draw your attention to the 13th of July. Can you please describe what happened on that day?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC
utterances.text: On the 13th, in the morning, I believe it was around 10.00 in the morning, commander General Mladic arrived in the Viogor sector, together with General Krstic, and there were also all the commanders of the units of tactical groups 1 and 2, the commanders that were on the strength of those units, and all the units that were deployed in the area were gathered to attend that rally.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. And where did that occur?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC
utterances.text: In the camp, in the premises of our unit, in the camp at the Viogor pass.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Do you know why it is that Mladic, General Mladic, was there that day?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC
utterances.text: General Mladic directly issued orders to the unit to get ready for a march towards the Zepa sector.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And had you heard any prior -- of any prior discussion about his arrival on the 13th, before then, before his actual arrival?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC
utterances.text: General Krstic had hinted at that on the previous day, when he told us that it would be General Mladic who would be issuing direct orders to us. So General Krstic indicated that.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Now, the previous day you mean the 12th of July?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, on the 12th.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And what if -- well, what do you recall General Mladic said, what the order was?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC
utterances.text: The long and the short of it would be this: Tactical groups 1 and 2 should be ready to start marching towards the Zepa sector and the mission was to continue combat activities and to eventually take the Zepa enclave.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And was there any, well, disagreement about the proposed mission or the order?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC
utterances.text: I don't remember that anybody but Commander Pandurevic disagreed. I can't remember anybody else disagreeing.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Well, what do you mean by that, if you could elaborate?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC
utterances.text: Well, to put it simply, Commander Pandurevic had a right to voice proposals or objections to any missions or tasks he might have received from his superior. He pointed out that the 28th Division had not been destroyed, that according to the reports that had been presented to us, the troops of the 28th Division could be found in the Jaglici sector, which was to the north from where we were, and that there was an objective possibility that they had been regrouped and getting ready to start breaking through towards the free territory of Tuzla. And if they did that, they would be in the Memici-Baljkovica-Petkovci sector and that they would be behind the Zvornik Brigade troops which would put the brigade in a rather unfavourable position if at the same time the forces coming from the front were acting together with the units of the 28th Division in order to link up, which would mean that the defence of that brigade would be at a risk and that maybe even several battalions of the Zvornik Brigade would suffer great consequences of all that.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And were you there when he pointed this out? Were you present?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And what if anything was the response by General Mladic?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC
utterances.text: The response was that the commander had received his orders, that he was supposed to carry it out, and that there were ample other forces which would prevent the 28th Division from crossing the Konjevic Polje-Kasaba-Milici road, that they would simply not be allowed to cross that road and that the commander should not have any concerns with that respect.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Now, did Commander Pandurevic point this out in front of the -- all of the other commanders that were there and all of the other people that had been gathered there or did this occur at some other location and time?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC
utterances.text: Everybody was there. The troops that were lined up in units and the closest to the general were the commanders, their immediate subordinates, and that's the way how we received our orders from the general.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: What happened after -- what happened after that?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC
utterances.text: All the commanders accepted the orders by saying that they understood them, and they went off to start preparing their troops for the march.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. Did you have any conversation with Commander Pandurevic about the order that General Mladic had issued?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC
utterances.text: Not the very -- the order itself, about going towards Zepa, but the Zvornik Brigade was our brigade, Zvornik was our town, we took it to our hearts. I personally did. I felt rather uncomfortable. I don't want to speak for the commander. I don't know what was on his mind. But I personally felt rather uncomfortable when I heard all that.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Well, did you discuss this with the commander?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, actually, yes, at the time, I did. But without any conclusions. Our orders were what they were, and we set out to carry them out in order to be able to arrive at the destination that were part of General Mladic's orders.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. After you prepared the troops to proceed according to the order, tell us what happened.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC
utterances.text: Once the unit was prepared, we started moving along the Viogor-Derventa-Milici-Vlasenica-Han Pijesak-Pozeplje axis. Before that, we replenished our units with ammunition and other materiel and technical equipment that would enable them to reach their destination without any impediments.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And how far did you get that night, that evening?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC
utterances.text: Around 2.00 in the morning on the 14th, we were in Rijeka village between Pozeplje and Han Pijesak.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. And is that where you spent the night, that night?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. That's where we spent the night, in the Rijeka village sector.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And during that day, did you have contact with the Zvornik Brigade?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC
utterances.text: No. We did not have any contact. The only thing I can remember is the fact that we spent some time in Vlasenica. At the petrol station which is at the entry into Vlasenica, we filled up the tanks of all of our vehicles, the passenger vehicles and the combat vehicles alike.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And do you know whether or not your commander had contact with the brigade that evening?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC
utterances.text: No, he didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I'm referring to Commander Pandurevic.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC
utterances.text: No. Commander Pandurevic did not have any contact with the command of the brigade in Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Can I ask, how do you know that?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC
utterances.text: I know for a very simple reason. We were together and we did not have an occasion to establish any contact with the brigade. There were a lot of vehicles, it was night, there were a lot of problems, breakdowns. We had to reach the destination in time envisaged by the order. We were even a bit delayed.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Well, did you express your concern or have a message conveyed to the brigade about your worries that you indicated you had as a result of General Mladic's order?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC
utterances.text: Are you referring to the unit that was there, that was under Pandurevic's command and in which I was the operative officer? You're not referring to the command of the Zvornik Brigade? I didn't understand who you were referring to.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I'll rephrase the question. First I'm talking about communication between your tactical group and the Zvornik Brigade. And my question is: Did you contact or try to contact the Zvornik Brigade to express your concerns or worries that you had as a result of the order that was issued by General Mladic?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC
utterances.text: No, sir, because General Mladic said that this was not our concern, that a command higher than the corps command would resolve that, would deal with that. As soon as he said that that was their problem and their thing to deal with, we all supposed that somebody must have assumed the full responsibility for the things that were spelled out by Commander Pandurevic as a possibility.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. You spent the night in Rijeka on the 13th of July?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC
utterances.text: Between the 13th and the 14th July, as from the very early morning hours of that night, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: On the 14th of July, can you tell us what you recall about that morning?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC
utterances.text: The commander -- actually, we had been given the task to prepare our unit to march to the Pozeplje village sector and the commander went to the forward command post of the corps that had been set up in the village called Krivaca.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And around what time did the commander go to the forward command post of the corps? And when you say corps, you mean the Drina Corps; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. It was the Drina Corps. It was in the early morning hours. I can't tell you exactly when, because we had our reconnoitring missions very early in the morning, and he did it upon having received his orders, the task that had been given to him.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Do you mean he received an order to go to the forward command post?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC
utterances.text: I suppose so. He would not have gone there without having been asked to. He would not just do it spontaneously. I mean, he can ask to be received there but it's usually upon being invited.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. And around what time did he return? How long was he away?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC
utterances.text: It didn't take him longer than an hour to go there, to receive his order, and to go back.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And did he tell you what his order was and from whom he received it?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC
utterances.text: He received an order from General Krstic, who was at the forward command post, as the person in command of all these operations. Our task was to leave the village of Pozeplje as our starting point and to mount an attack on the axis of Pozeplje-Brloznik-Purtici village in the direction of Zepa.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. And is that what you did following that?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC
utterances.text: After reconnoitring and drafting an action plan that we interpolated on to the map and showed to the unit in order for them to be able to mount this attack, the units launched the attack along the main axis of the attack. To the right-hand side was Tactical Group 2. On the auxiliary axis. And to the left of us was Tactical Group 1 of the Zvornik Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And how far did you get on the 14th of July?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG DRAGUTINOVIC
utterances.text: Because we took the village of Brloznik and once we arrived on the slopes which are above the village of Purtici, it was already late in the afternoon or early evening, and this is where our units spent the night. This is where we stopped our action. And there was also lateral activity from the Brlog mountain that we had to neutralise, which means that on the slopes of the hill above Purtici, the tactical group troops stopped and stayed with a view to continuing their mission on the following day.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. That's where they stopped, and this is where we stop. We are adjourned until tomorrow morning at 9.00. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
